brief:
Today is Pull B if you train — that is where the six-day order sits. Every number on your cards is exactly the one that was there yesterday, and that is on purpose. You have not logged a session since 2 September, so there is no new evidence, and re-deriving your weights from the same log every morning is how this app once produced four different answers in a week off one set of facts.

You should know today's review ran short-handed. Of your three trainers only the load trainer finished. The recovery trainer and the program trainer both failed to start — the machine that runs them stalled, four times for one and twice for the other, and I could not get either to report. That is a fault on my end, not a judgement about your training. It matters for one reason and I want to say it out loud: the recovery trainer is the only one who can stop a lift on safety grounds, and nobody sat in that seat this morning. What makes tonight all right anyway is that not one number moved. Every weight below was argued out by all three trainers yesterday and cleared then. If you had trained since, I would not have shipped this.

Now the thing that keeps getting bigger. You have not trained legs in sixteen days. Last Legs A was 20 August; last Legs B was 16 August, twenty days ago. Five sessions have run since and every one was push or pull. The order will offer you Pull B tonight because that is where the rotation sits, not because legs are handled. If you want tonight to be a leg day instead, the plan screen lets you set the day by hand and the order carries on from there. That is your call to make on purpose rather than by default.

Still open from yesterday, and I have no answer yet. On 2 September you wrote "New gym. No smith machine." Pull B opens with the Smith Bent-Over Row. If you are at that gym tonight, that card describes a machine you cannot reach — do the closest row you can get to and log what you actually lift, and the app will learn from that. And I still need to know whether the new gym is now your gym or whether you were passing through. Your chest press has been logged at three different scales in twelve days: 165 to 180 at your usual place, 67.5 to 75 on the Hammer Strength on 23 August, 97.5 to 157.5 on 2 September. Those are three machines wearing one name. If the new place is permanent, the honest move is to re-baseline the program there rather than have me keep quoting weights from a building you have left.

Tonight's numbers, if you run Pull B. Two lifts that had been stuck move. Incline curl goes to 30-pound dumbbells for two sets of eight — now that the slot is two sets rather than three, both surviving sets hit ten at 25 every single time, which is the top of the range, and the third set was the only thing ever falling short. Cable reverse curl goes to 38.75, which is 37.5 plus one small add-on, for three sets of ten, because eleven-eleven-eleven at 37.5 has happened twice running and asking for a twelfth rep has failed both times. Face pulls go to 30 for two sets of twelve off 27.5 for fifteen and fifteen on 28 August.

Three hold their weight and ask for reps instead. Close-grip pulldown stays at 127.5 wanting ten on all three — your third set fell to eight last time and that is the only thing between you and 135. Straight-arm pulldown stays at 45 wanting twelve, one more than the eleven you have hit three times. Shrugs stay at 80 wanting thirteen; 80s are the heaviest pair on that rack, so reps are the only road left.

Housekeeping. Your bodyweight has not been logged since 23 August, thirteen days ago, and has sat at 206 to 207 since July. With the show on 1 March that trend is the one number I cannot get from anywhere else, so step on the scale this week. Easy cardio twice this week, twenty to thirty minutes.

Meso 2, week 2 of 4, a build block. Nothing new has been logged since 2 September, so tonight's numbers are unchanged from yesterday's review by design.

proposals.why: The cable lateral raise is the only side-delt work on Push A and it has drifted to seventh of eight — on 27 August the session ended after the sixth exercise, so your side delts got nothing that night while your rear delts got all three sets; this moves it up to fifth, straight after the shoulder press, so it happens before the tail of the session rather than after it.

overrides.reason: On 25 August you hit ten reps — the top of the range — on all four rungs at 115, 135, 145 and 150, so the whole ramp goes up five pounds. Unchanged from yesterday because nothing new has been logged. If there is no smith machine where you are tonight, this card does not apply: do the nearest row you can and log that instead.
The weight stays at 127.5 because your third set dropped to eight last time even after a full two minutes' rest. Ten on all three is what buys 135, and this machine's next step is a full 7.5.
Eleven, eleven and eleven at 45 on 25 August — one rep short of the top of the range on every set, so tonight asks for the twelfth before it asks for more weight.

Twelve, twelve and twelve at 80 is the bottom of the range on your first outing at that weight, and 80s are the heaviest pair on the rack, so this asks thirteen at the same dumbbells rather than repeating twelve.

Now that this is two sets instead of three, both remaining sets have hit ten at 25 every time — the top of the range — and it was only the third set that ever fell short. That earns the next dumbbell up, so 30 for two sets of eight. If you cannot reach eight on both, that is the answer and we go back to 25 needing ten and ten.

Eleven, eleven, eleven at 37.5 on both 15 and 25 August. Asking for a twelfth rep has failed twice, so instead this adds the smallest weight the machine owns — one 1.25 add-on, making 38.75 — and re-enters at ten.
On 28 August you did 27.5 for fifteen and fifteen, the top of the range on both sets, so this steps up by the small add-on weights to 30 and re-enters at twelve.

panel.note: The recovery and program seats failed to start — the harness stalled on dispatch (recovery four attempts, program two). Neither reported, so no seat held veto authority today. Every number in this packet is identical to the 2026-09-04 packet, which a full three-seat panel ruled on against the same evidence; nothing new has been logged since 2026-09-02.
